title: Welcome back, 2016
gist: Ben Ansell argues populism is proving unpopular in power (Trump losing both houses of Congress, Orbán and Vučić defeated, Reform UK slipping as it governs councils) and that Britain is 'Breversing' at pace after Andy Burnham declared Brexit a failure; using a Prohibition analogy he projects a 2027 election on rebuilding EU ties and a possible 2032 campaign to end Brexit.

insights.claim: Ben Ansell argues populism is proving not to be popular, particularly when in power, citing Donald Trump losing both houses of Congress in the 2026 US midterms.
insights.speaker: Ben Ansell
insights.so_what: Suggests a cyclical turn away from populist governance across Western democracies, lowering tail risks from radical policy.

insights.claim: Andy Burnham's September speech to Labour conference was reported mainly for tackling the pensions triple lock, but Ansell says the bigger, undercovered news was his declaration that Brexit failed.
insights.speaker: Ben Ansell
insights.so_what: A sitting prime minister calling Brexit a failure is a regime shift for UK-EU policy; watch UK assets sensitive to EU market access.

insights.claim: Ansell notes Brexit closely tracks US Prohibition a century earlier: both took off in the mid-2010s/1910s, Prohibition came into force in January 1920 and Brexit in January 2020, and Prohibition became unpopular by the mid-1920s before FDR ran on repeal in 1932 and ended it in 1933.
insights.speaker: Ben Ansell
insights.so_what: Offers a rough timeline for policy reversal: popular disillusion precedes political courage to repeal by several years.

insights.claim: If history rhymes, Burnham would fight a 2032 general election on ending Brexit the following year, with a 2027 general election fought on rebuilding ties with Europe ahead of re-entry.
insights.speaker: Ben Ansell
insights.so_what: Implies a multi-year path of incremental UK-EU reintegration, with a 2027 election as a near-term marker.
insights.quote: If history rhymes further, that would mean Burnham running a 2032 general election with a plan to end Brexit the following year.

insights.claim: Ansell argues Brexit failed to produce the economic boom or national pride its proponents promised, making it possible to 'unscramble this particular egg'.
insights.speaker: Ben Ansell
insights.so_what: Economic underperformance is the driver of reversal; a rejoin trajectory is a medium-term upside case for sterling.
